# Anthropic - Manager of Applied AI Architecture, Partnerships briefing packet
| Manager of Applied AI Architecture, Partnerships | $315,000–$380,000 USD | Reports to Partnerships (partner-led applied AI architecture) |

## JD Complement
Anthropic’s public identity combines AI safety research with commercial deployment of Claude. This creates a distinct field reality: partners need enough technical freedom to build repeatable customer solutions, while staying within a
company whose differentiation is reliability, security, and steerability.

The operating tension is not simply adoption versus technical complexity. It is standardizing partner-delivered deployment patterns without turning Claude into a loosely governed implementation layer whose quality, security, or safety
posture varies by partner.

## Company DNA & Operating Model
Anthropic is a public benefit corporation and AI safety and research company building reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. Its commercial motion is a hybrid of product-led AI platform adoption and ecosystem-led enterprise
deployment.

Claude is the core commercial surface, positioned as an assistant for complex work such as analysis, coding, writing, and problem solving. That makes Anthropic’s enterprise opportunity less about a single application sale and more about
embedding a general-purpose AI capability into customer workflows.

The company’s central operating challenge is to translate frontier-model capability into trusted, repeatable business outcomes while preserving the safety-centered product identity that differentiates Anthropic in a crowded AI market.

## Company Strategy & Operating Pressure
Anthropic’s strategy carries an inherent dual mandate: advance capable AI systems and make them dependable enough for broad organizational use. Reliability, interpretability, steerability, accuracy, and security are not peripheral messages;
they are central to the company’s stated positioning.

Its commercial model must therefore support both end-user product adoption and deeper implementation through enterprise technology environments. The decision-rights pressure is likely around where reusable product patterns end and
partner-specific solution work begins.

For partnerships, the strategic value is leverage. Services, cloud, and technology partners can extend reach into customer environments, but they also create a need for clear technical standards, solution boundaries, feedback loops, and
escalation paths.

## Leadership & Stakeholder Map
Anthropic publicly presents itself as a company spanning researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders. That multidisciplinary foundation matters commercially because enterprise deployment decisions can carry product,
security, policy, and reputational implications simultaneously.

The most material stakeholder map is likely to span:
- Cloud, technology, and services partners that influence where and how Claude is deployed.
- Commercial teams responsible for customer adoption and ecosystem growth.
- Product and engineering teams receiving structured deployment feedback.
- Research, safety, security, and policy functions that shape acceptable deployment boundaries.
- Customer technical and executive sponsors seeking production outcomes, not model demonstrations.

The role’s influence will depend on aligning these groups around reusable partner motions rather than relying on one-off technical heroics.

## AI, Data, Platform, Architecture Signals
Anthropic positions Claude as safe, accurate, and secure, with use cases spanning complex analysis, coding, and knowledge work. This signals that partner architecture must address practical workflow integration, not only model selection or
prompt design.

Anthropic’s company-level emphasis on interpretability and steerability raises the bar for solution design. Partners need to understand how to frame dependable human-and-AI workflows, define use-case boundaries, and communicate responsible
deployment practices to customers.

The durable architecture opportunity is likely in repeatable patterns around enterprise access, application integration, evaluation, operational controls, and adoption design. The role sits close to the point where product capabilities
become customer-operable systems.

## Partnership / Ecosystem Motion
Anthropic publicly maintains a partner network spanning cloud, technology, and services partners. This is meaningful ecosystem DNA, not merely a referral channel: each category contributes a different part of enterprise adoption.

Cloud partners can shape infrastructure availability and route-to-market. Technology partners can place Claude within broader application and data ecosystems. Services partners can convert platform capability into industry workflows,
implementation capacity, and change-management coverage.

The important commercial motion is therefore a connected co-sell and co-delivery system. High-value partnership work should make partner technical teams more independently effective while preserving a shared standard for solution quality
and customer outcomes.

Joint solution development is especially relevant where reusable patterns can be packaged for repeated customer problems. The strategic objective is not partner activity for its own sake; it is scalable adoption with a consistent Claude
experience.

## Recent Events & Urgency
Anthropic’s public partner ecosystem signals an operating shift from model access alone toward broader enterprise adoption through cloud, technology, and services channels.

That shift creates urgency to codify how partners represent, deploy, and support Claude. As enterprise AI buyers seek practical production use cases, the competitive advantage increasingly depends on time to value, technical confidence, and
the consistency of partner-delivered outcomes.

The pressure is amplified by the category itself: AI platforms can be evaluated quickly, but durable enterprise expansion depends on implementation quality, governance confidence, and credible ecosystem capacity.

## apps_rg Positioning Themes (targeting only, not proof)
- Partner-led enterprise AI adoption across cloud, technology, and services ecosystems.
- Technical co-sell leadership that connects account strategy to deployment feasibility.
- Repeatable reference architectures and enablement programs rather than bespoke demonstrations.
- Production AI implementation with attention to reliability, security, evaluation, and governance.
- Joint solution development that turns customer patterns into scalable partner offerings.
- Cross-functional translation between commercial priorities, customer requirements, and product feedback.
- Leadership of technical customer-facing teams in ambiguous, rapidly evolving platform environments.
- Executive communication that preserves technical rigor while accelerating adoption.

## apps_lic Outreach Angles (targeting only, not proof)
- Anthropic’s safety-centered product positioning makes partner implementation quality commercially consequential.
- The cloud, technology, and services partner network suggests a deliberate ecosystem-scale adoption strategy.
- Claude’s breadth across analysis, coding, and knowledge work creates an opening for reusable workflow patterns.
- The interesting problem is enabling partner independence without fragmenting customer experience or technical standards.
- A relevant conversation can center on how partner feedback becomes product signal, not just field escalation.
- The role sits at the intersection of technical credibility, ecosystem leverage, and responsible enterprise deployment.

The JD and this briefing are targeting inputs only. Candidate claims must come from the governed resume/proof graph.

Location: San Francisco, CA | New York City, NY | Seattle, WA

About Anthropic
Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

About the role
As the Manager of the Partnerships Applied AI Solutions Architect team, you will drive adoption of frontier AI by enabling deployment of Anthropic’s products (Claude for Enterprise, Claude Code, API) through our Global and Regional System Integrators, cloud partners (AWS, GCP, Azure), and strategic technology partners.

You will build and lead a team of Partner Solutions Architects, establish processes and best practices for partner-led pre-sales engagements, and represent Anthropic as the technical lead on its most important partnerships. In collaboration with Sales, Partnerships, Product, and Engineering, you will help partners incorporate leading-edge AI into their practices, accelerate indirect revenue, and execute long-term GTM strategy while maintaining our best-in-class safety standards.

Responsibilities
- Team Leadership & Development: Hire, manage, and mentor a team of Partner Solutions Architects. Set goals, run reviews, and coach each team member toward high productivity and career growth.
- Strategic Technical Partnership: Act as the senior technical thought partner to Anthropic’s GTM partnerships team. Co-build partner strategy with aligned GTM leadership, drive key programs, and align cross-functional stakeholders (Sales, Product, Engineering) behind partner outcomes.
- Partner Enablement & Ecosystem: Embed your team with GSI and cloud partner technical teams to enable their AI practices, troubleshoot, and evangelize Anthropic in their developer communities. Represent Anthropic at partner events (GSI workshops, AWS/GCP summits, hackathons) and contribute technical content and thought leadership.
- Joint Solution Development: Lead partners in identifying high-value, industry-specific GenAI applications. Develop joint solutions and codify reference architectures and best practices to accelerate time to deployment.
- Customer Deal Support: Own the technical portion of partner-led pre-sales engagements. Intervene directly on strategic deals where partners are the primary delivery vehicle, providing deep solution architecture guidance.
- Product Feedback: Gather and validate feedback on Anthropic’s products from partner deployments and deliver it to Product and Engineering to inform roadmap and partner strategy.

You may be a good fit if you have
- 7+ years in technical customer-facing or partner-facing roles (Solutions Architect, Sales Engineer, Partner SE, TAM).
- 3+ years managing pre-sales or partner-facing technical teams; comfortable building foundational teams in ambiguous, fast-moving environments.
- Track record building and scaling partnerships with GSIs (e.g., Accenture, Deloitte, TCS, Infosys) and/or cloud providers (AWS, GCP, Azure).
- Deep understanding of partner-led selling and delivery: indirect revenue models, enablement at scale, and joint GTM motions.
- Technical depth in enterprise AI deployments: LLM architecture, prompt engineering, evaluation, API integrations, and production use cases.
- Exceptional communication and executive presence; able to build trusted relationships with C-suite, partner leadership, and engineering teams alike.
- A love of teaching and mentoring, and a passion for advancing safe, beneficial AI.

Strong candidates may also have
- 5+ years leading partner-facing SA teams through hypergrowth, including developing both senior and junior talent.
- Direct experience helping GSIs or consultancies build their AI/ML practice - enablement programs, certification paths, joint solution development.

Annual Salary: $315,000 - $380,000 USD

Logistics
Minimum education: Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience.
Required field of study: A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience.
Minimum years of experience: Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position.
Location-based hybrid policy: Currently, Anthropic expects all staff to be in one of its offices at least 25% of the time. Some roles may require more time in office.
Visa sponsorship: Anthropic says it sponsors visas but cannot successfully sponsor every role and candidate.
"
}

# Anthropic - Manager of Applied AI Architecture, Partnerships briefing packet
| Manager of Applied AI Architecture, Partnerships | $315,000–$380,000 USD | Reports to Partnerships (partner-led applied AI architecture) |

## JD Complement
Anthropic’s public identity combines AI safety research with commercial deployment of Claude. This creates a distinct field reality: partners need enough technical freedom to build repeatable customer solutions, while staying within a
company whose differentiation is reliability, security, and steerability.

The operating tension is not simply adoption versus technical complexity. It is standardizing partner-delivered deployment patterns without turning Claude into a loosely governed implementation layer whose quality, security, or safety
posture varies by partner.

## Company DNA & Operating Model
Anthropic is a public benefit corporation and AI safety and research company building reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. Its commercial motion is a hybrid of product-led AI platform adoption and ecosystem-led enterprise
deployment.

Claude is the core commercial surface, positioned as an assistant for complex work such as analysis, coding, writing, and problem solving. That makes Anthropic’s enterprise opportunity less about a single application sale and more about
embedding a general-purpose AI capability into customer workflows.

The company’s central operating challenge is to translate frontier-model capability into trusted, repeatable business outcomes while preserving the safety-centered product identity that differentiates Anthropic in a crowded AI market.

## Company Strategy & Operating Pressure
Anthropic’s strategy carries an inherent dual mandate: advance capable AI systems and make them dependable enough for broad organizational use. Reliability, interpretability, steerability, accuracy, and security are not peripheral messages;
they are central to the company’s stated positioning.

Its commercial model must therefore support both end-user product adoption and deeper implementation through enterprise technology environments. The decision-rights pressure is likely around where reusable product patterns end and
partner-specific solution work begins.

For partnerships, the strategic value is leverage. Services, cloud, and technology partners can extend reach into customer environments, but they also create a need for clear technical standards, solution boundaries, feedback loops, and
escalation paths.

## Leadership & Stakeholder Map
Anthropic publicly presents itself as a company spanning researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders. That multidisciplinary foundation matters commercially because enterprise deployment decisions can carry product,
security, policy, and reputational implications simultaneously.

The most material stakeholder map is likely to span:
- Cloud, technology, and services partners that influence where and how Claude is deployed.
- Commercial teams responsible for customer adoption and ecosystem growth.
- Product and engineering teams receiving structured deployment feedback.
- Research, safety, security, and policy functions that shape acceptable deployment boundaries.
- Customer technical and executive sponsors seeking production outcomes, not model demonstrations.

The role’s influence will depend on aligning these groups around reusable partner motions rather than relying on one-off technical heroics.

## AI, Data, Platform, Architecture Signals
Anthropic positions Claude as safe, accurate, and secure, with use cases spanning complex analysis, coding, and knowledge work. This signals that partner architecture must address practical workflow integration, not only model selection or
prompt design.

Anthropic’s company-level emphasis on interpretability and steerability raises the bar for solution design. Partners need to understand how to frame dependable human-and-AI workflows, define use-case boundaries, and communicate responsible
deployment practices to customers.

The durable architecture opportunity is likely in repeatable patterns around enterprise access, application integration, evaluation, operational controls, and adoption design. The role sits close to the point where product capabilities
become customer-operable systems.

## Partnership / Ecosystem Motion
Anthropic publicly maintains a partner network spanning cloud, technology, and services partners. This is meaningful ecosystem DNA, not merely a referral channel: each category contributes a different part of enterprise adoption.

Cloud partners can shape infrastructure availability and route-to-market. Technology partners can place Claude within broader application and data ecosystems. Services partners can convert platform capability into industry workflows,
implementation capacity, and change-management coverage.

The important commercial motion is therefore a connected co-sell and co-delivery system. High-value partnership work should make partner technical teams more independently effective while preserving a shared standard for solution quality
and customer outcomes.

Joint solution development is especially relevant where reusable patterns can be packaged for repeated customer problems. The strategic objective is not partner activity for its own sake; it is scalable adoption with a consistent Claude
experience.

## Recent Events & Urgency
Anthropic’s public partner ecosystem signals an operating shift from model access alone toward broader enterprise adoption through cloud, technology, and services channels.

That shift creates urgency to codify how partners represent, deploy, and support Claude. As enterprise AI buyers seek practical production use cases, the competitive advantage increasingly depends on time to value, technical confidence, and
the consistency of partner-delivered outcomes.

The pressure is amplified by the category itself: AI platforms can be evaluated quickly, but durable enterprise expansion depends on implementation quality, governance confidence, and credible ecosystem capacity.

## apps_rg Positioning Themes (targeting only, not proof)
- Partner-led enterprise AI adoption across cloud, technology, and services ecosystems.
- Technical co-sell leadership that connects account strategy to deployment feasibility.
- Repeatable reference architectures and enablement programs rather than bespoke demonstrations.
- Production AI implementation with attention to reliability, security, evaluation, and governance.
- Joint solution development that turns customer patterns into scalable partner offerings.
- Cross-functional translation between commercial priorities, customer requirements, and product feedback.
- Leadership of technical customer-facing teams in ambiguous, rapidly evolving platform environments.
- Executive communication that preserves technical rigor while accelerating adoption.

## apps_lic Outreach Angles (targeting only, not proof)
- Anthropic’s safety-centered product positioning makes partner implementation quality commercially consequential.
- The cloud, technology, and services partner network suggests a deliberate ecosystem-scale adoption strategy.
- Claude’s breadth across analysis, coding, and knowledge work creates an opening for reusable workflow patterns.
- The interesting problem is enabling partner independence without fragmenting customer experience or technical standards.
- A relevant conversation can center on how partner feedback becomes product signal, not just field escalation.
- The role sits at the intersection of technical credibility, ecosystem leverage, and responsible enterprise deployment.

deployment.

Claude is the core commercial surface, positioned as an assistant for complex work such as analysis, coding, writing, and problem solving. That makes Anthropic’s enterprise opportunity less about a single application sale and more about

- Commercial teams responsible for customer adoption and ecosystem growth.
- Product and engineering teams receiving structured deployment feedback.

About Anthropic
Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

About the role
As the Manager of the Partnerships Applied AI Solutions Architect team, you will drive adoption of frontier AI by enabling deployment of Anthropic’s products (Claude for Enterprise, Claude Code, API) through our Global and Regional System Integrators, cloud partners (AWS, GCP, Azure), and strategic technology partners.

You will build and lead a team of Partner Solutions Architects, establish processes and best practices for partner-led pre-sales engagements, and represent Anthropic as the technical lead on its most important partnerships. In collaboration with Sales, Partnerships, Product, and Engineering, you will help partners incorporate leading-edge AI into their practices, accelerate indirect revenue, and execute long-term GTM strategy while maintaining our best-in-class safety standards.

Responsibilities
- Team Leadership & Development: Hire, manage, and mentor a team of Partner Solutions Architects. Set goals, run reviews, and coach each team member toward high productivity and career growth.
- Strategic Technical Partnership: Act as the senior technical thought partner to Anthropic’s GTM partnerships team. Co-build partner strategy with aligned GTM leadership, drive key programs, and align cross-functional stakeholders (Sales, Product, Engineering) behind partner outcomes.
- Partner Enablement & Ecosystem: Embed your team with GSI and cloud partner technical teams to enable their AI practices, troubleshoot, and evangelize Anthropic in their developer communities. Represent Anthropic at partner events (GSI workshops, AWS/GCP summits, hackathons) and contribute technical content and thought leadership.
- Joint Solution Development: Lead partners in identifying high-value, industry-specific GenAI applications. Develop joint solutions and codify reference architectures and best practices to accelerate time to deployment.
- Customer Deal Support: Own the technical portion of partner-led pre-sales engagements. Intervene directly on strategic deals where partners are the primary delivery vehicle, providing deep solution architecture guidance.
- Product Feedback: Gather and validate feedback on Anthropic’s products from partner deployments and deliver it to Product and Engineering to inform roadmap and partner strategy.

You may be a good fit if you have
- 7+ years in technical customer-facing or partner-facing roles (Solutions Architect, Sales Engineer, Partner SE, TAM).
- 3+ years managing pre-sales or partner-facing technical teams; comfortable building foundational teams in ambiguous, fast-moving environments.
- Track record building and scaling partnerships with GSIs (e.g., Accenture, Deloitte, TCS, Infosys) and/or cloud providers (AWS, GCP, Azure).
- Deep understanding of partner-led selling and delivery: indirect revenue models, enablement at scale, and joint GTM motions.
- Technical depth in enterprise AI deployments: LLM architecture, prompt engineering, evaluation, API integrations, and production use cases.
- Exceptional communication and executive presence; able to build trusted relationships with C-suite, partner leadership, and engineering teams alike.
- A love of teaching and mentoring, and a passion for advancing safe, beneficial AI.

Strong candidates may also have
- 5+ years leading partner-facing SA teams through hypergrowth, including developing both senior and junior talent.
- Direct experience helping GSIs or consultancies build their AI/ML practice - enablement programs, certification paths, joint solution development.

Annual Salary: $315,000 - $380,000 USD

Logistics
Minimum education: Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience.
Required field of study: A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience.
Minimum years of experience: Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position.
Location-based hybrid policy: Currently, Anthropic expects all staff to be in one of its offices at least 25% of the time. Some roles may require more time in office.
Visa sponsorship: Anthropic says it sponsors visas but cannot successfully sponsor every role and candidate.
"
}
